correctness.rationale: Baslingker–Virág Theorem 5 already proves the exact directed-cycle Fourier variational representation of B_K under equal marginals. For t active coordinate frequencies each has energy ≥sin²(π/K), so t≥3 has quotient ≤1/(t sin²(π/K)). For exactly two, sin²(a+b)=sin²a+sin²b+2sin(a)sin(b)cos(a+b), bounding quotient by 2cos²(π/K) for K≥4 with equality from two K-cycles. Thus B2=B3=B4=1, B5=(3+√5)/4, B6=3/2. For K≥4, principal angles δ_i∈[α,π/2], α=π/K, satisfy sin²δ_i/δ_i≥sin²α/α; the nearest-to-π signed sum s≤Σδ_i yields B_K≤α/sin²α * max_{0≤s≤π/2}sin²s/s. The maximum occurs at unique τ∈(0,π/2) solving tanτ=2τ. Taking n=floor(τK/π) unit-frequency K-cycles attains the limiting slope sin²τ/(πτ). Independent numerical direct evaluations at K=5,6 agree; finite checks do not prove the limit.
